body.estimand_functional: \(Q_{a,H}=F_H(p_H)\quad\text{for }p_H\in\mathfrak D_H=\{q:q(c)>0\text{ for each branch-required cell and }d_{H,r}(q)>0\text{ for every registered reduced denominator}\}\), on the formula branch only

sampling_model.design: Units are sampled independently from the single joint law \(p_H(V,S)\), whose selector support is exactly the declared finite set \(H\); the algorithm never constructs a context outside that set.
sampling_model.units: Observed units are i.i.d. draws of \((V,S)\); latent roots and response types are not observed.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed treatment components may be natural or selector-overridden according to the known gate encoded by \(S\); the target sets \(A=a\) and \(S=s_{\emptyset}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every structurally admissible supported cell is strictly positive. Each context normalizer, chain-rule conditioning marginal, actual nested-fixing conditional, and accepted elimination divisor used by a returned formula is recorded in a step-indexed ledger and proved positive by induction. No common numerical lower bound and no positivity outside \(H\) are imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On a formula branch, estimate the finite table \(p_H\) empirically and evaluate the returned rational circuit only on its ledger-projected domain \(\mathfrak D_H\). Pointwise Wald inference is valid at each fixed differentiable interior law with positive target variance. A pending residual is an algorithmic certificate gap, not a point estimate or a nonidentification conclusion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algorithms 1--2 are sound, specified failure branches imply nonidentification, and completeness is conjectured.
Ordinary semi-Markovian ID is complete through identifying formulas or hedge countermodels.
Positive gID is sound and complete by reduction to classical ID subproblems.
Root-control CSI identification is equivalent to finitely many ordinary graphical identification problems.
Finite canonical SCMs represent all categorical counterfactual distributions and yield sharp polynomial-program bounds.
The arithmetic-circuit method is at least as complete as classical ID and do-calculus under strict positivity and can exploit additional model constraints.
Sufficient pruning and transit-clustering conditions preserve identification conclusions and transport do-calculus functionals.
Influence-function and weight-based estimators are derived for broad classes of identified effects in hidden-variable graphical models.

body.tldr: For finite selector-gated semi-Markovian SCMs observed on exactly \(H\), retained support normalization and a deterministic Algorithms 1--2 task machine preserve every successful support-licensed formula, certify every actual division, and terminate at a sound formula, a verifier-accepted support-exact twin, or an explicitly pending residual. The all-residual rational-formula-or-global-twin dichotomy remains the sole missing step, so the field completeness headline is preserved but is not claimed as proved.

project_justification.gap: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser give a sound systematic-selection recursion and witnesses for specified failures, but not an input-determined fixed-support execution semantics or an all-residual exact-support converse. The redesigned machine closes the execution gap without importing a successful trace; residual candidate exhaustiveness alone remains open.
project_justification.niche: The setting fixes one coherent joint selector law on exactly \(H\). Supported contexts share natural mechanisms and selector provenance, while absent contexts cannot be invoked. This differs from ordinary observational ID and from data-fusion formulations that supply separate experiments.
project_justification.fill: The proved layer supplies intrinsic support normalization, canonical finite graph computations, explicit recursive work tasks, computed valid fixing sequences, distinct truncated factorization and fixing, a step-indexed positivity ledger, multiset termination, positive-branch preservation, sound formula and twin verification, pointwise interior inference, and an ordinary-ID structural specialization. The intended field result additionally requires the open all-residual rational-projection-or-global-contrast theorem.

body.related_work: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser (2024) provide the selector-gated model and Algorithms 1--2. The present positive result is a line-by-line, input-determined refinement: every graph, context, closure, fixing sequence, hybrid factor, and denominator is computed from the finite input and current state, and every successful support-licensed branch is preserved. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) provide the ordinary ID formula-or-hedge endpoint; the new machine specializes structurally to that recursion when the selector is constant and separated. Tabell, Tikka, and Karvanen (2026) give pruning and clustering for general data fusion but no fixed-support parameter-image converse. The remaining novelty claim is confined to exact-support residual exhaustion, which is still open.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Nonresidual circularity is removed: initialization, closure, contexts, conditional-independence tests, fixing orders, hybrid products, spawned district work, and denominator proofs are finite deterministic computations. The unresolved issue is semantic rather than operational: it is unknown whether every generated residual has a rational identifying projection or a common rational-affine response contrast preserving all supported observed descendants. Boundary-uniform inference and unrestricted quantifier elimination remain outside scope.
body.honest_scope: Proved here are support normalization, input determinacy, computed closure and fixing, local context and kernel identities, step-indexed denominator positivity, no-stuck nonresidual progress, multiset termination, preservation of successful published positive formulas, certificate soundness, the binary Algorithm-2 residual certificate, pointwise interior Wald inference, and ordinary-ID structural reduction. The formula-or-global-twin completeness theorem remains open exactly through \(\textnormal{oeq:all-residual-dichotomy}\); no LGS failure tag is promoted to nonidentification without a verified global twin, and no absent selector context is supplied.
body.interpretation: A positive output is an explicit rational map of the supplied joint selector table, together with every denominator needed to evaluate it. A verifier-accepted negative output is an open rational family of canonical SCM pairs sharing the entire admissible observed law and exact selector support while disagreeing on the intervention target. An LGS failure tag or ResidualPending output carries neither conclusion by itself.
